$comment: Export projection for a tenant site.db. The unit of reproducibility is this projection, not the file: two VACUUM INTO copies of the same logical content are not byte-identical once any volatile table has a row (scripts/model/verify_claims.py check 8). 'rows' = data travels; 'empty' = the table exists in the bundle and carries no rows. A table missing from this file is a build failure, so a new table cannot join the schema without someone deciding what it means for a sale.

cms_settings.filter: key NOT GLOB 'demo.*' AND key NOT GLOB 'billing.*'
cms_settings.why: Site configuration travels; operator-only namespaces (demo furniture, billing state) do not. Without the filter a bundle exported from a demo goes live wearing the demo banner and noindex tag (Red Team O2).

cms_page_revision.why: The undo history is part of the handover: the client's first action after install is usually to fix a typo we made.

cms_nav.why: The site is unusable without its navigation.

cms_asset.why: Media library. Gated rows are refused by the exporter before this projection is applied (Platform refusal GATED_ASSETS_PRESENT).

cms_asset_alias.why: Old keys must still 301 inside the client's instance, or every URL we ever published to them dies at handover.

cms_asset_variant.why: Derived files, but the rows are the index of which files exist; regenerating them all on install is minutes of CPU on a box we do not control.

cms_asset_link.why: The usage graph; without it 'delete this image' stops warning about the page that uses it.

cms_asset_bundle.why: A sellable set is content, not commerce state.

cms_download_code.why: Purchaser emails, order refs and live code fingerprints. A sold bundle has no issuers and no buyers; carrying the rows hands the client our customer list and our live codes (Red Team O3).

cms_download_event.why: ip_hash/ua_hash are personal data collected for our forensics, and the rows are per-request volatile, so they break reproduction as well.

cms_watermark_render.why: One stamped file per purchaser, each carrying a different buyer's email. It is the single largest PII store in the file and the one that grows without bound (Red Team O12).

cms_form.why: Form definitions are part of the site.

cms_form_submission.why: Prospect PII from our sales pipeline, not the client's content (Red Team O3). A CMS sold to the same client can export with --include-submissions, which is an explicit operator decision with an audit row.

cms_datasource.why: The site's data bindings; a page whose source is missing renders an empty region.

cms_view_registry.why: Views are migration-owned and the DDL postcondition reads this table; a bundle without it fails its own integrity check.

cms_table_registry.why: The u_* inventory. EXPORT-NOTES.md must state its row count (Runtime contract).

cms_audit.why: Our operators' actions and labels. The client starts with an empty audit log, which is honest: we did not do anything on their box yet.

cms_redirect.why: Redirects are content; dropping them 404s every slug we renamed during the build.
